# TCP

## Reliable delivery

The Transmission Control Protocol provides reliable, ordered delivery of a stream of bytes between two hosts. A connection is established with a three-way handshake before any data is sent. Each segment carries a sequence number so the receiver can put the data back in order. The receiver sends acknowledgements, and the sender retransmits a segment if no acknowledgement arrives in time.

## Congestion and flow

TCP controls how fast a sender transmits by using a congestion window. During slow start the window grows quickly, roughly doubling every round trip. When packet loss is detected, the sender reduces its window to relieve congestion. Flow control is separate from congestion control and prevents a fast sender from overwhelming a slow receiver. In contrast, UDP does not guarantee delivery or ordering.
